Fehu: Fehu (ᚠ) is the rune of wealth, resources, and moving abundance. It represents what you possess, what you can create, and the responsibility that comes with having something of value. Wealth is never entirely still — it grows, changes hands, and demands movement.
Uruz: Uruz (ᚢ) is the rune of raw power, strength, and primal force. It speaks of the vitality that rises before it has a name or a direction — the body's own strength, the will to endure. Power of this kind is not yet shaped; its task is to be directed, not to be tamed away.
Thurisaz: Thurisaz (ᚦ) is the rune of the gateway, the threshold, and the thorn. It marks a place where caution is wise: what protects can also wound, and what disrupts can also open the way. It asks you to pause at the threshold and look before you cross.
Ansuz: Ansuz (ᚨ) is the rune of messages, wisdom, and the voice. It is breath given meaning — the word spoken, the guidance received, the thing you finally hear. It points to communication, understanding, and the quiet moment when a message arrives.
Raidho: Raidho (ᚱ) is the rune of the road, of movement and natural rhythm. It is not only the journey but the right way of making it: the correct action at the correct pace. Progress here comes from moving in step with the road, not from hurrying it.
Kenaz: Kenaz (ᚲ) is the rune of the torch and of inner light. It stands for creativity, knowledge, and the fire that lets you see and shape what is in front of you. A flame that is kept gives light to the one who carries it, and warmth to others.
Gebo: Gebo (ᚷ) is the rune of the gift, of companionship and of balance. It describes giving and receiving as one movement — nothing offered without something returning. It speaks of bonds that hold because both sides give.
Wunjo: Wunjo (ᚹ) is the rune of joy, happiness, and harmony. It speaks of belonging, of a wish fulfilled, and of the ease that comes when things are in their right place. It is the quiet gladness of being among your own.
Hagalaz: Hagalaz (ᚺ) is the rune of hail — disruption that arrives from outside and cannot be negotiated with. It stands for transformation and clearing: what is struck down makes room for what comes after. It is the force of nature at its least gentle and most honest.
Nauthiz: Nauthiz (ᚾ) is the rune of necessity and need. It names the constraint that presses on you and the growth that can come only through that pressure. What you lack shows you what you need, and difficulty is often where strength is made.
Isa: Isa (ᛁ) is the rune of ice, of stillness and waiting. Everything holds; nothing moves. It asks for a pause, and offers clarity through cold — the kind of seeing that is only possible when the water stops running.
Jera: Jera (ᛃ) is the rune of the harvest and the turning year. It speaks of cycles, patience, and right timing: what was sown is gathered when it is ready, not before. Reward here follows steady work and the willingness to wait for the season.
Eihwaz: Eihwaz (ᛇ) is the rune of the yew tree — resilience and endurance. It is often linked with the world-tree and with death and rebirth, for the yew stands through winters that end other things. It stands for protection, and for what holds when everything else gives way.
Perth: Perth (ᛈ) is the rune of chance and the unseen. It stands for the hidden coming to light, for luck, and for fate in the making. Its meaning is deliberately open: something is still being decided, and not everything is yet visible.
Algiz: Algiz (ᛉ) is the rune of protection and shelter. It stands for higher powers and for the connection to something greater than yourself. It is the open hand raised toward the sky, and the sense of being guarded while you stay watchful.
Sowilo: Sowilo (ᛊ) is the rune of the sun, of victory and life force. It brings clarity and will — the energy that burns away doubt and lights the way ahead. Solar energy of this kind rewards the one who walks toward it.
Tiwaz: Tiwaz (ᛏ) is the rune of justice, sacrifice, and truth. It is the warrior spirit in its disciplined form: courage that serves a cause larger than the self. It asks what you are willing to give up to stand by what is right.
Berkana: Berkana (ᛒ) is the rune of the birch — of growth, new beginnings, and birth. It is the rune of nurturing: patient care for something small that will become larger. The first tree to green after the cold, it asks for gentleness and time.
Ehwaz: Ehwaz (ᛖ) is the rune of the horse, of movement and trust. It speaks of partnership between two who move as one, and of progress that is made together. Trust is the reins and the road at once.
Mannaz: Mannaz (ᛗ) is the rune of the self and of humanity. It stands for self-awareness, the mind, and your place among other people. To know yourself is to know what you share with everyone else.
Laguz: Laguz (ᛚ) is the rune of water — flow, intuition, and the unconscious. It carries emotion, memory, and dreams: the deep things that move beneath the surface. It asks you to trust the current and to listen to what rises from below.
Ingwaz: Ingwaz (ᛜ) is the rune of the seed and of inner development. It speaks of fertility and potential gathered quietly before it shows. What is incubating inside is still unseen, but it is new life in the making.
Othila: Othila (ᛟ) is the rune of inheritance, home, and heritage. It stands for ancestral wisdom and the foundation you stand on, and also for letting go of what no longer serves. Belonging is built from what you keep and what you release.
Dagaz: Dagaz (ᛞ) is the rune of the turning point and the dawn. It speaks of breakthrough — the moment light replaces dark and transformation becomes visible. Day does not come by force; it arrives, and everything looks different.
Blank: The Blank rune (○) stands for the unknown and for unwritten potential. It is the void before the first mark, and is tied to destiny. Some link it to Odin. It carries no fixed meaning: it asks you to stay open to what has not yet been decided.
